issues.title: FK creation missing validation for referenced UNIQUE/PK requirement
issues.evidence: . No requirement that the referenced parent column(s) must be PRIMARY KEY or have a UNIQUE index, which SQLite requires for referenced columns.
issues.recommendation: In the FK creation dialog, add an explicit validation step: (1) detect whether the chosen parent column(s) are covered by a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE index; (2) if not, block creation with a clear error and offer an optional flow to create a UNIQUE index on the parent column(s) (or force the user to do it via SQL editor). Also specify behavior when parent table is WITHOUT ROWID or has composite PKs (even if creation remains single-column-only).
issues.acceptanceTest: Checklist/E2E: Create parent table P(a INT) with no PK/UNIQUE; child C(p_a INT). In ERD, attempt FK C.p_a → P.a. Verify: creation is blocked with message explaining
. Then create UNIQUE index on P(a) (via offered action or SQL editor), retry, verify FK is created and PRAGMA foreign_key_list(C) shows it. Add explicit E2E id (e.g., E2E-US-004-05).

issues.title: IndexedDB fallback serialization/restore mechanics are underspecified (risk of unimplementable or memory-heavy fallback)
issues.evidence: No explicit mechanism is defined for how serialization is performed with wa-sqlite/WASM (e.g., sqlite3_serialize vs VACUUM INTO vs VFS copy), nor memory/perf implications.
issues.recommendation: Specify the exact serialization and restore approach for fallback mode, including memory bounds. Example: use SQLite's sqlite3_serialize/sqlite3_deserialize (if supported by the build) OR `VACUUM INTO` to an OPFS/temporary file then read as Blob, and on load write Blob to an in-memory VFS file before opening. Define the expected peak memory behavior (since full-DB snapshots can require >= DB size in memory) and any size caps or warnings specific to fallback (beyond the 50MB recommendation).
issues.acceptanceTest: Unit/Integration: In fallback mode, run: create DB, insert data, trigger a write, wait for debounce, verify IndexedDB contains blob; hard reload; verify data restored. Perf gate: for a 25MB fixture in fallback mode, snapshot save completes within a defined time bound and does not exceed a defined heap ceiling (recorded via Playwright trace/metrics). Add a failure-mode test: simulate serialization failure and verify the 3-retry + modal behavior occurs as specified.

issues.title: “Case-insensitive LIKE” depends on SQLite PRAGMA and collation; current spec may not be deterministic
issues.evidence: . SQLite LIKE case-sensitivity can be affected by `PRAGMA case_sensitive_like` and locale/NOCASE behavior.
issues.recommendation: Make the filter semantics deterministic by specifying SQL generation explicitly, e.g., `WHERE <col> LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\' COLLATE NOCASE` (ASCII-ish) or `WHERE lower(<col>) LIKE lower(?) ESCAPE '\\'` (more consistent but may affect indexes). Also specify whether the app sets/assumes any PRAGMAs (and whether the SQL editor can change them).
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E: Ensure filter finds 'AbC' when searching 'abc' regardless of PRAGMA changes. Test: set `PRAGMA case_sensitive_like=ON` via SQL editor, then apply UI filter; verify it still behaves case-insensitively. Confirm generated SQL contains the chosen deterministic mechanism (COLLATE NOCASE or lower()).

issues.title: SQL editor “error with line number reference” is not precisely defined for multi-statement scripts
issues.evidence: and E2E-US-005-03 expects a mid-script error with line number. Execution model: multi-statement prepare loop; SQLite errors typically lack a reliable line number.
issues.recommendation: Define the line/column mapping strategy: at minimum, report the statement index + starting line number (computed by counting newlines before the prepared statement start offset). Optionally add best-effort column by scanning token position near `sqlite3_errmsg`
hint. Update acceptance criteria to match what is actually measurable/testable.
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E: Paste a 3-statement script with an error in statement 2; verify UI shows
and a computed line range or starting line. Add unit test for the offset-to-line mapping function with a few tricky inputs (comments, semicolons in strings).

issues.title: “Preview the generated DDL diff” needs a concrete definition to be testable and consistent across designer/ERD
issues.recommendation: Specify the diff format and content: show (a) original CREATE TABLE SQL, (b) proposed CREATE TABLE SQL, and (c) a unified diff view (optional). Define what else is included (indexes/triggers/FKs if rebuilt) and whether identifiers are normalized for display.
issues.acceptanceTest: Checklist: For an FK add via ERD that triggers rebuild, the preview must include modified CREATE TABLE plus any dropped/recreated indexes/triggers, and a
summary. E2E: assert the preview contains both old/new CREATE TABLE strings and mentions the specific FK clause being added/edited.

issues.title: Keyset pagination criteria are ambiguous; duplicates can cause skipped/duplicated rows without stable ordering rules
issues.evidence: It doesn’t define how “unique column” is detected/validated, nor the stable secondary sort to ensure deterministic paging.
issues.recommendation: Define keyset eligibility and stable ordering: only enable keyset when ORDER BY is exactly (a) rowid, or (b) a NOT NULL UNIQUE/PK column. Always add a deterministic tie-breaker (e.g., `ORDER BY sort_col, rowid`) when possible. If the sort column can have duplicates and isn’t unique, force OFFSET/LIMIT or require a secondary unique key.
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E: Create table with duplicate values in a non-unique column, sort by that column, scroll through virtualization fetches; verify no duplicates/missing rows across fetch boundaries. Unit: `isKeysetEligible(orderBy)` returns true only for rowid/unique-not-null columns and generates correct SQL with tie-breaker.

issues.title: OPFS registry self-heal conflict resolution depends on “most recently modified” which may be inconsistent across environments
issues.recommendation: Define exactly how “most recently modified” is obtained in OPFS (e.g., via `handle.getFile().lastModified`) and the fallback when timestamps are equal/unavailable (e.g., pick lexicographically first and suffix the other). Also specify whether this conflict resolution applies in IndexedDB mode (where modification times may not exist).
issues.acceptanceTest: Unit: given two entries with same-case-insensitive name and missing timestamps, deterministically resolve using documented tie-breaker. Integration: create `MyDB.sqlite` and `mydb.sqlite` (simulated) and verify startup produces one active name and one `(conflict)` renamed entry with a console log as specified.

issues.title: Quota-exceeded detection and UX is specified, but the trigger conditions/error mapping are not
issues.evidence: It does not define how quota errors are detected (which errors from OPFS/SQLite/IndexedDB map to “Storage full”).
issues.recommendation: Add a mapping table for storage-full conditions: OPFS write failures (DOMException names), SQLite IO errors returned by wa-sqlite, IndexedDB quota errors, and how they surface to the UI. Include a requirement that the quota modal is shown only once per session per DB unless state changes (to avoid toast storms).
issues.acceptanceTest: Fault-injection test: simulate quota errors (mock OPFS/IndexedDB failure or force small quota in test harness) and verify (1) writes are blocked across UI entry points, (2) SQL script is rolled back, (3) modal shows correct message, (4) exports/deletes remain enabled.

issues.recommendation: Make US-006 E2E language consistent: either assert exact SQL string (preferred given deterministic requirement) or keep “pattern” and loosen determinism/testing claim accordingly.

suggestions.title: Add a “Reset all local data” / “Factory reset” flow
suggestions.description: You have per-DB delete, but not a one-click way to wipe everything (OPFS/IndexedDB registry, databases, metadata, localStorage query histories). This is useful for debugging, demos, and privacy hygiene.
suggestions.recommendation: that deletes OPFS directory (or enumerates and deletes contents), clears IndexedDB stores, and clears relevant localStorage keys (`qh:*`). Require a typed confirmation (e.g., type DELETE).
suggestions.rationale: Improves trust and testability, and reduces support burden when users get into odd states (corrupt registry, conflicts, etc.).

suggestions.title: Define a consistent error taxonomy + user-facing messages
suggestions.description: Many flows mention “clear error” (invalid DB, corrupted, quota, dependency breakage). A shared taxonomy prevents inconsistent UI strings and makes E2E assertions cleaner.
suggestions.recommendation: Create an error code map (e.g., ERR_DB_INVALID_HEADER, ERR_DB_ENCRYPTED, ERR_QUOTA, ERR_DEPENDENCY_BROKEN) with prescribed user messages and optional technical details drawer (raw SQLite error).
suggestions.rationale: Reduces ambiguity, improves UX consistency, and makes failures easier to triage.

suggestions.title: Add “Open read-only” option on import/open
suggestions.description: Sometimes users want to inspect without risk, especially when OPFS auto-imports and persistence is automatic.
suggestions.recommendation: that opens with `SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY`, disables write entry points, but still allows export. Persist the read-only flag per DB in registry metadata (optional).
suggestions.rationale: Improves safety and matches common DB tooling patterns without adding backend complexity.

suggestions.title: Specify schema introspection caching policy (even if v1 is “no cache”) with a measurable UX target
suggestions.description: This is fine, but it’s worth adding a UX threshold for DB switching so it doesn’t regress unnoticed.
suggestions.recommendation: Add a simple metric: switching active DB (with <=200 tables) should populate sidebar tree within X ms (e.g., 500ms) on baseline environment, measured in E2E/perf suite. Keep
suggestions.rationale: Prevents death-by-a-thousand-cuts performance regressions in the navigation experience.

suggestions.title: Constrain v1 table-rebuild “SQL textual comparison” to a clear allowlist of clauses
suggestions.description: The rebuild guardrails are ambitious: parse + reproduce + textual compare after normalization. This can balloon complexity and still be brittle.
suggestions.recommendation: Define an explicit allowlist of table-level features that must be preserved and verified via PRAGMAs where possible; use textual checks only for the handful of clauses without PRAGMA coverage (and document exactly which).
suggestions.rationale: Keeps the guardrail strong while avoiding an open-ended SQL “equivalence” problem.

suggestions.title: Add accessibility acceptance checks for core interactions (grid, ERD, query editor)
suggestions.description: Drag/drop + canvas UIs are common accessibility failure zones; adding a minimal set of a11y gates early avoids expensive retrofits.
suggestions.recommendation: Add: keyboard navigation for grid editing, focus management for modals, and at least one non-drag alternative for creating FKs (e.g., dialog-based selection). Include axe-core checks in Playwright for critical screens.
suggestions.rationale: Improves usability and reduces risk for a desktop-first professional tool.

strengths: Exceptionally concrete acceptance criteria with E2E IDs throughout; this is unusually implementation-friendly.
Clear v1 boundaries (supported vs not supported) across designer, ERD, and query builder, reducing scope creep risk.
Strong durability model for OPFS VFS direct mode with explicit guarantees and UI state semantics (Saved/Unsaved).
Thoughtful handling of risky schema operations: transactional rebuild, dependency detection, and rollback guardrails.
Good performance discipline: defined baseline environment, measurable budgets, and CI measurement approach (CDP heap sampling, traces, Lighthouse CI).
Security section is pragmatic and relevant for a client-only app (escaping, CSP, worker isolation, parameterization, formula-injection protection).
Data interchange rules are precise (NULL vs empty string semantics, RFC 4180 behaviors, BOM handling), which prevents painful “CSV surprises.”
Multi-tab single-writer policy is explicitly designed with hard backstops (`SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY`) and UI-level disabling.

overallAssessment.summary: The PRD is detailed and largely testable, with strong performance/security/persistence thinking. Address the two major gaps (FK referenced-key validation and IndexedDB snapshot mechanics) plus a handful of minor determinism clarifications, and implementation should proceed with low rework risk.
